To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) the POR gene is up-regulated by cyclophosphamides and (2) this may be a mechanism for the interindividual variation of the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of cyclophoshamide.
the POR gene can influence the bioactivation of cyclophophamide, and that the POR gene expression is up regulated in patients after cyclophophamid infusion.
The activity of the CYP2B enzyme is dependent on the activity of POR and that the expression of POR is influenced by cyclophosphamides itself.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of POR in the activation of the chemotherapeutic drug cyclophosphamides.
the development of new methods to improve personalized medicine.

the development of new methods for the analysis of the metabolism of the anti-cancer drug cyclophosphamid and the identification of the genetic factors that determine the variability in the pharmacokinetics and toxicity of the drug.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
both the POR and the CYP genotype as well as their expression levels are important to achieve an optimal therapeutic effect of cyclophophamide.
the POR/CYP expression ratio is a key factor for cyclophosphamides bioactivation.
both CYPs and POR expression and/or function may influence cyclo-phosphamide bioactivation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
POR and CYP2B expression levels are important factors for cyclophosphamides bioactivation.
the ratio of POR/CYP is important to predict the in vitro metabolism of cyclophophamide.
the POR gene is a novel candidate gene for the inter-individual variation in the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of cyclophophamide.
The main takeaway from our work is that
POR and CYP2B genotype and expression levels have to be taken in account when individualizing treatment schedules to reach optimal cyclophosphamid concentrations.
the POR/CYP expression ratio is important in cyclophophamide activation and thus, POR genotype and expression levels should be considered when personalizing treatment regimens.
the POR genotype may be an important determinant of CYP2C9 and CYP2B metabolism, and that this may be relevant to drug interactions.
